entries.name: Stat Block Overview
entries: A monster has a stat block that contains the rules necessary to use it in the game. Stat blocks are divided into the following parts, which correspond with the example stat block, Vampire Familiar:

items.name: Name and General Details
items.entry: The name of the monster is followed by its size, creature type (along with any descriptive tags), and alignment.

items.name: Combat Highlights
items.entry: {@variantrule Armor Class|srd52}, {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}, {@variantrule Speed|srd52}, and {@variantrule Initiative|srd52} are provided here.

items.name: Ability Scores
items.entry: A monster's ability scores, ability modifiers, and saving throws are listed here.

items.name: Other Details
items.entry: The monster's Senses, Languages, and CR entries appear here. Additional details appear in some monsters, such as skill proficiencies, Resistances, Immunities, and Gear. If a monster lacks those details, entries for them don't appear.

items.name: Traits
items.entry: Monster characteristics that are active at all times or during certain situations appear here.

items.name: Actions
items.entry: The monster can take the actions here in addition to those in "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}".

items.name: Bonus Actions
items.entry: This section provides a monster's Bonus Actions, if any.

items.name: Reactions and Legendary Actions
items.entry: These sections provide Reactions and Legendary Actions, if any. The example monster doesn't include these parts.

entries.name: Parts of a Stat Block
entries: The rules for a stat block are detailed in "{@book Rules Glossary|srd52|9}" and in this section.

entries.name: Size
entries: A monster is Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, or Gargantuan. If size options are presented, you choose the creature's size from those options. See "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}" for information on size.

entries.name: Creature Type
entries: Each monster has a tag that identifies the type of creature it is. Certain spells, magic items, class features, and other effects in the game interact in special ways with creatures of a particular type.
The game includes the following creature types, which have no rules of their own:

items.name: {@filter Aberrations|bestiary|type=aberration}
items.entry: are utterly alien beings, such as aboleths, beholders, flumphs, and mind flayers.

items.name: {@filter Beasts|bestiary|type=beast}
items.entry: are non-Humanoid natural creatures, like horses and wolves, as well as most giant animals.

items.name: {@filter Celestials|bestiary|type=celestial}
items.entry: are magical creatures, such as angels and pegasi, with ties to the Upper Planes.

items.name: {@filter Constructs|bestiary|type=construct}
items.entry: are magically created creatures such as homunculi, modrons, and shield guardians.

items.name: {@filter Dragons|bestiary|type=dragon}
items.entry: are scaly beings of ancient origin, such as red dragons and wyverns.

items.name: {@filter Elementals|bestiary|type=elemental}
items.entry: are beings from the Elemental Planes, such as efreet and water elementals.

items.name: {@filter Fey|bestiary|type=fey}
items.entry: are creatures tied to the Feywild or the forces of nature, such as dryads, goblins, and pixies.

items.name: {@filter Fiends|bestiary|type=fiend}
items.entry: are creatures tied to terrifying Lower Planes, such as balors and hell hounds.

items.name: {@filter Giants|bestiary|type=giant}
items.entry: are towering beings with humanlike shapes, like cyclopes, fire giants, and trolls.

items.name: {@filter Humanoids|bestiary|type=humanoid}
items.entry: are people defined by their roles and professions, such as mages, pirates, and warriors. They include members of varied species.

items.name: {@filter Monstrosities|bestiary|type=monstrosity}
items.entry: are unnatural creatures with strange origins, such as mimics and owlbears.

items.name: {@filter Oozes|bestiary|type=ooze}
items.entry: are gelatinous creatures, including black puddings and blobs of annihilation.

items.name: {@filter Plants|bestiary|type=plant}
items.entry: are sentient vegetation and fungal monsters, such as myconids, shambling mounds, and treants.

items.name: {@filter Undead|bestiary|type=undead}
items.entry: are spirits and the reanimated dead, such as ghosts, vampires, and zombies.

entries.name: Descriptive Tags
entries: A monster might have one or more tags in parentheses following its type. Such tags provide additional categorization and have no rules of their own, but certain game effects might refer to them.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: The alignment specified in a monster's stat block is a default suggestion of how to roleplay the monster, inspired by its traditional role in the game or real-world folklore. Change a monster's alignment to suit your storytelling needs. The Neutral alignment, in particular, is an invitation for you to consider whether an individual leans toward one of the other alignments.
"{@book Character Creation|srd52|2}" describes the nine alignments and unaligned creatures.

entries.name: Armor Class
entries: A monster's {@variantrule Armor Class|srd52} (AC) includes its natural armor, Dexterity, gear, and other defenses. See "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}" for information on Armor Class.

entries.name: Initiative
entries: The {@variantrule Initiative|srd52} entry specifies the monster's {@variantrule Initiative|srd52} modifier followed by the monster's {@variantrule Initiative|srd52} score in parentheses. Use the modifier when you roll to determine a monster's {@variantrule Initiative|srd52}. A monster's {@variantrule Initiative|srd52} modifier is typically equal to its Dexterity modifier, but some monsters have additional modifiers, such as {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus}, applied to that number.

If you don't want to roll a monster's {@variantrule Initiative|srd52}, use the {@variantrule Initiative|srd52} score as the monster's {@variantrule Initiative|srd52} in combat. Initiative is further detailed in "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}".

entries.name: Hit Points
entries: A monster's {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52} are presented as a number followed by parentheses, where the monster's {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|srd52} are provided, along with any contribution from its Constitution. Either use the number for the monster's {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52} or roll the die expression in parentheses to determine the monster's {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52} randomly; don't use both.
A monster's size typically determines the die used to calculate its {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}, as shown in the Hit Dice by {@variantrule Size|srd52} table.

A monster's Constitution modifier is multiplied by the number of Hit Dice it possesses, and the result is added to its {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52}. For example, if a monster has a Constitution of 12 (+1 modifier) and {@dice 2d8} Hit Dice, it has {@dice 2d8 + 2} {@variantrule Hit Points|srd52} (average 11).
For more on Hit Points, see "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}".

entries.name: Speed
entries: The Speed entry specifies a monster's Speed. Some monsters have one or more of the following speeds: {@variantrule Burrow Speed|srd52|Burrow}, {@variantrule Climb Speed|srd52|Climb}, {@variantrule Fly Speed|srd52|Fly}, {@variantrule Swim Speed|srd52|Swim}. Rules for Speed and these specials speeds appear in "{@book Rules Glossary|srd52|9}".

entries.name: Ability Scores
entries: Every monster has six ability scores along with corresponding ability score modifiers and saving throw modifiers. For more information on ability scores and saving throws, see "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}".

entries.name: Skills
entries: The Skills entry specifies a monster's skill proficiencies, if any. For example, a monster that is very perceptive and stealthy might have bonuses to Wisdom ({@skill Perception|srd52}) and Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|srd52}) checks. A skill bonus is the sum of a monster's relevant ability modifier and its {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus}. Other modifiers might apply.

entries.name: Resistances and Vulnerabilities
entries: These entries list a monster's Resistances and Vulnerabilities, if any. See "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}" for more information.

entries.name: Immunities
entries: This entry lists the monster's {@variantrule Immunity|srd52|Immunities}, if any. If the monster has damage and condition Immunities, the damage types are listed before the conditions. See "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}" for details.

entries.name: Gear
entries: Monsters have proficiency with their equipment. If a monster has equipment that can be given away or retrieved, the items are listed in the Gear entry. The monster's stat block might include special flourishes that happen when the monster uses an item, and the stat block might ignore the rules in "{@book Equipment|srd52|6}" for that item. When used by someone else, a retrievable item uses its "{@book Equipment|srd52|6}" rules, ignoring any special flourishes in the stat block.
The Gear entry doesn't necessarily list all of a monster's equipment. For example, a monster that wears clothes is assumed to be dressed appropriately, and those clothes aren't in this entry.
Equipment mentioned outside the Gear entry is considered to be supernatural or highly specialized, and it is unusable when the monster is defeated.

entries.name: Ammunition and Ranged Attacks
entries: A monster that requires ammunition to make ranged attacks carries the necessary ammunition.

entries.name: Equipping a Monster with Other Items
entries: You may equip monsters with additional gear however you like, using the items in "{@book Equipment|srd52|6}" for inspiration. You decide how much of a monster's equipment is recoverable after the creature is slain and whether any of that equipment is still usable.

Beware of giving a monster combat-oriented magic items, since those might alter the monster's {@variantrule Challenge Rating|srd52}. If you do give a monster a magic item, the monster can have {@variantrule Attunement|srd52} with magic items as noted in "{@book Equipment|srd52|6}". A monster with a class tag after its creature type is considered a member of that class for {@variantrule Attunement|srd52} purposes.

entries.name: Running a Monster
entries: To ensure a monster acts in accordance with its {@variantrule Challenge Rating|srd52}, follow these rules during combat:

items.name: Special Abilities
items.entry: If the monster has a special ability that deals a lot of damage but has a limited number of uses, such as a recharging breath weapon or a spell it can cast only once per day, have it use that special ability as quickly and as often as possible.

items.name: Multiattack
items.entry: If the monster has Multiattack, have it use Multiattack on any of its turns in which it's not using one of its more powerful abilities.

items.name: Bonus Actions, Reactions, Legendary Actions
items.entry: If the monster has Bonus Actions, Reactions, or Legendary Actions in its stat block, make sure it uses them as often as it can.

entries.name: Senses
entries: The Senses entry specifies a monster's {@variantrule Passive Perception|srd52} score, as well as any special senses the monster possesses. Passive Perception and special senses are described in "{@book Rules Glossary|srd52|9}".

entries.name: Languages
entries: This entry lists languages that the monster can use to communicate. Sometimes a monster can understand a language but can't communicate with it, which is noted in its entry. "None" indicates that a creature doesn't comprehend any language.

entries.name: Telepathy
entries: Telepathy is a magical ability that allows a creature to communicate mentally with another creature within a specified range. See "{@book Rules Glossary|srd52|9}" for more information.

entries.name: Challenge Rating
entries: Challenge Rating is defined in "{@book Rules Glossary|srd52|9}", while guidance on using CR to plan potential combat encounters is in "{@book Gameplay Toolbox|srd52|10}".

entries.name: Experience Points
entries: The number of {@variantrule Experience Points|srd52} (XP) a monster is worth is based on its CR, as detailed in the {@variantrule Experience Points|srd52} by {@variantrule Challenge Rating|srd52} table. XP is awarded for defeating the monster in combat or otherwise neutralizing it.
Unless a rule says otherwise, a monster summoned by a spell or another magical ability is worth the XP noted in its stat block.

entries.name: Proficiency Bonus
entries: A monster's {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus} (PB) is determined by its CR, as shown in the {@variantrule Proficiency|srd52|Proficiency Bonus} by {@variantrule Challenge Rating|srd52} table, and is reflected in saving throws, skills, and other statistics where the monster's exceptional aptitude is a factor.

entries.name: Traits
entries: A monster's traits, if any, are features that are active at all times or in certain situations.

entries.name: Actions
entries: A monster can take the actions in this section or take one of the actions available to all creatures, as described in "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}".

entries.name: Attack Notation
entries: The entry for a monster's attack identifies whether the attack is a melee or a ranged attack and then provides the attack roll's bonus, its reach or range, and what happens on a hit. An attack is against one target unless its entry says otherwise. For details on different kinds of attacks, see "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}" and "{@book Spells|srd52|7}".

entries.name: Hit
entries: Any damage dealt or other effects that occur as a result of an attack hitting a target are described after the "Hit:" notation.

entries.name: Miss
entries: If an attack has an effect that occurs on a miss, that information follows the "Miss:" notation.

entries.name: Hit or Miss
entries: If an attack has an effect that occurs regardless of whether it hits or misses its target, that information follows the "Hit or Miss:" notation.

entries.name: Saving Throw Effect Notation
entries: If an effect forces a saving throw, the effect identifies the kind of save required and then provides the save's DC, a description of which creatures make the save, and an explanation of what happens on a failed or successful save.
"Half damage only" on a successful save means the target takes half as much damage (round down) as targets that fail the save, while also ignoring all other parts of the effect.

entries.name: Damage Notation
entries: A stat block usually provides both a number and a die expression for each instance of damage. For example, an attack might deal 4 ({@damage 1d4 + 2}) damage on a hit. You decide whether to use the number or the die expression in parentheses; don't use both.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries: Some creatures can make more than one attack when they take the {@action Attack|srd52} action. Such creatures have the Multiattack entry in the "Actions" section of their stat block. This entry details the attacks a creature can make, as well as any additional abilities it can use, as part of the {@action Attack|srd52} action.

entries.name: Spellcasting
entries: If a monster can cast any spells, its stat block lists the spells and provides the monster's spellcasting ability, spell save DC (if any spells require a saving throw), and spell attack bonus (if any spells require an attack roll). Unless noted otherwise, a spell of level 1 or higher is always cast at its lowest possible level and can't be cast at a higher level.

A monster's spell can have special rules or restrictions. For example, a green hag can cast the {@spell Invisibility|srd52} spell, but the spell has a "self only" restriction, which means the spell affects only the hag.

entries.name: Spell Components
entries: The Spellcasting trait notes whether the monster's spellcasting ignores the need for certain spell components. If any spell components are required, describe the monster's use of Verbal, Somatic, or Material components to signal to characters that it is casting a spell. A monster that requires Material components has them.

entries.name: Casting Times of 1+ Minutes
entries: If a spell has a casting time of 1 minute or more yet is listed in a spellcasting action, the monster doesn't cast the spell in just one action unless the action's description states otherwise; the monster must take the {@action Magic|srd52} action on each of its turns and maintain {@status Concentration|srd52} to cast the spell, as described in "{@book Rules Glossary|srd52|9}".

entries.name: Bonus Action
entries: If a monster has Bonus Action options, they are listed in this section. See "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}" for details on Bonus Actions.

entries.name: Reactions
entries: If the monster has Reaction options, those are listed in this section along with their triggers. See "{@book Playing the Game|srd52|1}" for details on Reactions.

entries.name: Legendary Actions
entries: If the monster has Legendary Action options, those are listed in this section. A Legendary Action is an action that a monster can take immediately after another creature's turn. Only one of these actions can be taken at a time and only after another creature's turn ends. The monster can't take a Legendary Action if it has the {@condition Incapacitated|srd52} condition or is otherwise unable to take actions.

The monster has a limited number of Legendary Action uses, and that number is specified in the stat block. The monster expends one use whenever it takes a Legendary Action, and it regains all expended uses at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Limited Usage
entries: Some parts of a stat block have restrictions on the number of times they can be used. Here are the most common ways that usage is limited:

items.name: X/Day
entries: This notation means the stat block part can be used a certain number of times (represented by X) and that a monster must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|srd52} to regain expended uses. For example, a {@variantrule Reaction|srd52} that includes "1/Day" means the {@variantrule Reaction|srd52} can be taken once and that the monster must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|srd52} to take it again.

items.name: Recharge X–Y
entries: This notation means a monster can use the stat block part once. At the start of each of the monster's turns, roll {@dice 1d6}. If the roll is within the number range given in the notation (represented by X–Y), the monster regains the use of that part, which also recharges when the monster finishes a {@variantrule Short Rest|srd52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|srd52}. For example, "Recharge 5–6" in an action means a monster can take the action once. Then, at the start of each of the monster's turns, it regains the use of that action if it rolls a 5 or 6 on {@dice 1d6}.

items.name: Recharge after a Short or Long Rest
entries: This notation means the monster can use the stat block part once and must then finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|srd52|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|srd52} to use it again.
